# Teacher Dashboard Analytics

Teacher Dashboard Analytics are visual tools designed to give educators clear, actionable insights into student learning progress within adaptive tutoring systems. These dashboards display mastery levels across subjects, highlight skill gaps, and track pacing relative to curriculum standards, enabling timely interventions.

Data is typically aggregated from student interactions with adaptive lessons, quizzes, and exercises. The dashboard updates in near real-time, using color-coded mastery indicators—green for proficient, yellow for developing, and red for struggling—to help teachers prioritize support. Filters allow viewing by class, subgroup, or individual student.

Tradeoffs include balancing detail versus simplicity: too much data can overwhelm, while too little risks missing nuanced learning issues. Additionally, data latency and accuracy depend on the underlying assessment design and student engagement.

For example, in Lincoln Middle School's 7th-grade math class, the dashboard shows 65% of students have mastered fractions (green), 25% are developing (yellow), and 10% are struggling (red). The teacher uses this to schedule targeted group sessions.

Common failures arise from incomplete data due to low student login rates or misaligned assessments failing to capture true mastery.
